title: OpenStack Sync Ironic Runbook Spec
description: Schema for Ironic runbook spec data consumed by openstack-sync. When attached to an IronicRunbook custom resource, only spec is constrained.

cloudCredentialsRef.description: Reference to a Kubernetes Secret containing the OpenStack clouds.yaml.

ironicRunbookSpec.description: Ironic runbook data stored under spec.

runbookName.description: Runbook name, and the identity the operator syncs by. Renaming creates a new runbook rather than renaming the existing one.

traits.description: Traits deciding which nodes this runbook may act on. A node must carry at least one; a runbook with no traits matches no nodes.

disableRamdisk.description: Whether to run without booting the cleaning ramdisk.

public.description: Whether every project can see the runbook. A public runbook cannot have an owner, and only a system-scoped credential can create one or set this on an existing runbook. Note that public governs visibility, not use: Ironic authorises a clean or service request against the runbook's owner alone, so a public runbook can be used only by a system-scoped or role:service token, never by a project-scoped one.

owner.description: Project that owns this runbook, and the only project whose manager or admin may use it. Unset leaves the field to Ironic, which fills it in for a project-scoped credential and leaves it empty for a system-scoped one; a runbook that is neither public nor owned can be seen and used by nobody. Removing this field from a CR does not clear an owner Ironic already assigned -- set public to true to clear it, which Ironic does itself. Moving a runbook between public and owned needs a system-scoped credential either way.

extra.description: Additional runbook metadata. The operator also keeps its ownership markers here, under _understack_runbook_ keys.

interface.description: Interface that owns this cleaning step.

step.description: Step name for the selected interface.

order.description: Execution order. Lower numbers run first.
